questions.question: Show with one example that subtraction of integers is not commutative.
questions.expected_answer: 5 − (−2) = 7 but −2 − 5 = −7; swapping the order changes the answer, so subtraction is not commutative.

questions.question: Verify the distributive property on −4 × (7 + (−3)) by evaluating it two ways.
questions.expected_answer: Bracket first: 7 + (−3) = 4, so −4 × 4 = −16. Distributing: −4 × 7 + (−4) × (−3) = −28 + 12 = −16. Both routes give −16.

questions.question: Why may you collect all the positives first in −3 + 8 + (−7) + 2, and what do you get?
questions.expected_answer: Addition of integers is commutative and associative, so terms may be reordered and regrouped. Positives 8 + 2 = 10, negatives −3 + (−7) = −10, total 0.
